newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ median house price falls in December.
newsitem.headline: NZ median house price falls in December.

text.p: The national median price for residential house sales was NZ$154,000 in December, down from $156,000 in November, figures released by the Real Estate Institute of New Zealand showed.
The median price was up 6.5 percent from the previous December.
REINZ said residential house sales eased slightly in December as prospective buyers waited for a predicted fall in interest rates.
Total house sales for the month reached 5,741, a decrease of 723 over the same period last year. November sales totalled 8,428 homes.

REINZ president Colin Brown said the drop in sales showed many buyers had been waiting to see if interest rates would fall after the Reserve Bank's monetary statement, which was released early in the month.
December was also traditionally a fairly slow month for property selling as people prepared for Christmas and the holiday break, he said.
The drop in sales was not significant and generally the market remained steady.
Brown said the December figures should not be taken as a guide to market prospects for 1997.

"I think we can expect an upturn in the January sales figures. With the recent lowering of interest rates we would anticipate increased interest from home buyers and more people looking at investment properties."
Sales in Auckland eased to 1,867, a drop of 474 over the same period last year, although the median sale price increased by $26,000 to $230,000.
Wellington reported a marked increase in sales, to 708, the highest for the past three years. The median price remained steady at $142,500.
The Wellington property market often set the trend for the rest of the country and the healthy figures were a positive indicator for the immediate future, Brown said.
